title: Fundamentals of Computer Science and Programming
abstract: The study course introduces students to the fundamentals of algorithm development and programming, demonstrating the possibilities of developing simple software solutions in C, Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS and SQL. The study course enables students to learn practical skills in the development of algorithms using different types of algorithm notation. The study course also includes topics on data structures, software development stages, as well as practical programming issues. An important part of the study course is made up by laboratory work, during which students learn the skills to use the knowledge acquired in the study course. The study course structure and learning materials are taken from Harvard University’s distance learning course CS50x. The study course is intended for students who do not specialize in the field of information and communication technologies.
aims: The aim of the study course is to teach students the fundamentals of algorithm development and programming to be able to perform simple tasks. Tasks of the study course: - to provide students with the knowledge, skills and competences to understand and apply algorithmic knowledge in order to solve various tasks; - to provide skills in using at least one integrated program development environment; - to develop skills to read and use program sample codes to solve simple tasks.
independent_study: In each practical class, students receive a task for practical implementation. Students start fulfilling the task in the nearest laboratory following its working hours and if they do not finish the task in the computer class, they do it independently.

title: Introduction to Engineering Sciences
status_in_programme: Compulsory/Courses of Limited Choice; Courses of Free Choice
abstract: The course aims to develop your identity in nowadays engineering and engineering sciences. The course provides insights into present-day engineering science divisions, technologies, and solutions, including modern data transmission and sensor network design, digital data transmission, and analysis. Nowadays, no engineering science is imaginable without Information and communication technologies (ICT). Students will be divided into groups during the course. Each of them will carry out laboratory works covering such essential topics in the ICT industry as network design, providing coverage in an object, the configuration of sensor networks, the processing, and analysis of received data. The laboratory works will be realized in the laboratory of the internet of things, using experience gained in vertically integrated projects (VIP) course regarding working with students lacking previous ICT knowledge and skills. Laboratory works will include detailed and precisely defined guidelines, descriptions, and instructions. The course also includes guest lectures led by representatives of leading research groups, (for instance, RTU ComTech, “RISE” – Sweden; TU/e Terahertz Photonic System Group – Netherlands, etc.) and leading companies (for example, “LMT”, ECO of Latvia, “MikroTik”, “Ubiquiti Networks”, “Siemens”, etc.), both recognized in Latvia and Europe.
aims: The objective of the course is to provide necessary theoretical and practical foundations in engineering sciences. Tasks of the course: • Familiarize with engineering and technological development history. • Comprehend current innovative solutions. • Generate and evaluate basic ideas. • Master engineering problem-solving methods. • Develop critical thinking about proposed engineering solutions regarding economic, environmental and social aspects. • Understand and cultivate technical writing. • Distinguish and practice professional ethics.
independent_study: During independent studies, students should use course materials form ORTUS, prepare for tests and tasks in the laboratory. Scenarios for independent learning are prepared using literature and hyperlinks to necessary web pages, covering course topics.

title: Digital Editing and Publishing
abstract: In the contemporary world, proofreaders and copyeditors are required not only in the academic and research environment, but also in the corporate business environment. The study course is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to work as professional writers, proofreaders, and copyeditors. Within the framework of the study course, students develop their research and critical thinking skills in writing, editing and publishing projects, acquire editorial principles and writing strategies in both print and digital media, as well as study the scientific publication life-cycle model. Students also develop an awareness of industry standards and requirements, and gain knowledge of designing and developing documents.
aims: The goal of the study course is to enable students to master the basic skills of proofreading and copyediting, and provide them with the skills necessary for project management in the publishing environment. The study course also aims at developing students’ skills to apply various digital editing tools in practice. The objectives of the study course: 1. to discuss with the students the role and scope of editing, recognizing the differences and similarities among a proofreader, editor and copyeditor; 2. to help students acquire professional codes of conduct; 4. to develop students’ competence to apply the software necessary for managing all stages of the publishing process; 5. to develop students’ ability to identify and correct common mistakes; 6. to advance students’ discourse organization skills.
independent_study: Students independently analyse different types of texts, identify and correct mistakes following the set requirements, as well as act as project managers guiding the content through each stage of the publishing process.

title: Research Strategies and Writing for Academic Publishing
abstract: In the study course, students will acquire skills and methods for writing scientific research texts in English for publication in internationally recognized academic journals. The study course discusses strategies for identifying relevant topics that match student interests and are of current research interest in student discipline. “Getting started strategies”, brainstorming method, reasons to publish, and identifying strategies and sources are discussed. During the course, students will develop a six to eight page article that they intend to publish. Since writing and re-writing is an integral part of manuscript production, students will present and discuss their drafts in class and give advice to colleagues. Each face-to-face session will address the research and writing process step by step.
aims: The aim of the study course is to teach to identify research projects relevant to interests and discipline. The tasks of the study course are: 1. To teach to formulate research questions and develop them into hypotheses. 2. To provide knowledge about relevant search strategies that include electronic and other sources. 3. To develop skills to describe research methods and explain how data will be collected and analysed. 4. To develop the ability to make a relevant literature review that identifies key studies relevant to research. 5. To teach to create an outline or mind-map to organize your writing. 6. To teach to write the first draft. 7. To teach to revise and edit your draft. 8. To teach to write an effective abstract. 9. To teach to give a PowerPoint presentation in a peer forum. 10. To teach to identify and avoid plagiarism.
independent_study: There will be two main class projects. Students will be expected to draft a six to eight page article in English that reflects the quality and uses a recognized scholarly referencing format. Students will also be expected to give a ten minute PowerPoint presentation on their research topic that displays quality and professionalism. The main weight of the evaluation will be based upon the professionalism of the article; its quality and originality and mastery of English and its feasibility for the public.

title: Graphic Design Technologies
abstract: The study course is designed for those E-humanities Masters and Bachelors degree students, who haven’t taken Digital Graphic design study course prior to their studies. The study course provides the necessary basic knowledge about Colour Theory, Basic Principles of Composition as page layouts and objects, typography for digital Graphic Design and insights in Visual Identity as a part of Visual Branding. Students got practical training to create basic graphic layouts via Adobe InDesign, they got acquainted with the main principles of vector graphic via Adobe Illustrator and acquires image manipulation basic skills in Adobe PhotoShop. Students acquire knowledge about main Graphic design file formats, their usage and characteristics, the principles of different styles in typography and harmonious colour palettes to build up the comprehension about the principles of Visual Identity. The core of the study course is based on the fundamental correlation between theory and practice –by obtaining knowledge via theory, demonstration of theory in practice in real work simultaneously is shown to students. During the study course, students are showing reflective practice by implementing their knowledge into the practice, building up their understanding that Graphic Design is the synthesis between student’s theoretical knowledge obtained and technical skills to use the software. Students are gaining expertise in Adobe InDesign, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe PhotoShop software by creating layouts, making image manipulation, drawing simple abstract vector shapes, and upon knowledge gained in composition, Colour Theory and Typography are creating their homework, final course project and passing an exam. After completion of the study course, students must be able to perform simple lay outing jobs, with basic knowledge in prepress file preparation in PDF file format for printing house and online; must create a basic composition and Colour palette for Visual Identity project, must make standard Graphic design file (.jpg,.tiff,.png,.ai, indd,.pdf) manipulations whether with self produced or outer obtained. The study course is designed to build up multidisciplinary effectiveness by helping non design professionals-students to build up presentation materials, whether it would be conference presentation or research presentation, work with images bought from the Image Stocks (Shutterstock, Adobe Stock, iStock and many more) for their promotion and professional purposes. The study course is especially advised for translators, media library workers, strategic communication specialists, scripters to help them with presentation papers to visually excel in the fast changing professional arena.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide knowledge and skills that allow students to create quality digital graphic material (body of the work). Objectives of the study course: 1. To provide with basic information about the principles of Digital Graphic Design Technologies - composition, Colour Theory, typography and their means of visual expression and usage in Adobe InDesign, Adobe Illustrator and Adobe Photoshop software. 2. To teach planning and creation of layout (with the help of Adobe InDesign) with bitmap images, vector images, typography with the usage of Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop technologies. 3. To provide students with the best practice for creating a layout. 4. To provide information and teach students to use the necessary tools to get the best results out by using composition, colour and typography. 5. To develop skills to create harmonious colour palettes, to look for compositional solutions, object interaction and placement solutions. 6. To develop skills to create quality layouts for prepress and online, basic knowledge to make image manipulation, whether the bitmap or vector ones, draw simple abstract vector shapes and compositions and implement them into the layout. 7. To develop skills to analyse own layout (body of work) from the perspective of composition, colour and typography. 8. To develop skills to generate ideas and to plan and create a mini Brandbook, as a mini Visual identity book in Adobe InDesign File format and be capable to make manipulations with bought or outsourced graphic design files for visual presentations.
independent_study: In order to successfully complete the study course programme and to pay attention to practical works by learning Adobe software in workshops, it must be assumed, that all students fully have studied online materials, like webinars, lecture notes and handouts and had prepared homework, tests prior to attending practical sessions to create independent Body of Work, to create a concept, to learn to make a layout, to make analyse the Work, to prepare Body of Work for the prepress and online.

title: Audio and Video Data Processing
abstract: During the study course, students will learn the filmmaking process from conception to publication. Students themselves will deal with the video production, including writing scripts, creating work plans, shooting and editing with the aim of establishing their own short film. Students will learn the basics of film planning, will gain skills in working with portable audio and video equipment, and learn to evaluate the composition, select the appropriate lighting and shoot material. In the post-production stage, students will learn the basics of video editing, they will learn to add graphic material, as well as prepare edited videos for publication on the web. With a view to preparing video of excellent quality, the study course will provide an overview of the latest tools for editing video and graphics and sound processing and effective methods of their application.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide knowledge and skills that allow the participants to create quality video material. The tasks of the study course: 1. to provide basic information on scriptwriting and means of visual expression in the video; 2. to teach planning and developing a video production plan; 3. to acquaint students with the best practice for managing video production 4. to provide information and teach students to select the necessary equipment, video cameras, lighting and sound equipment, video post-processing tools for video the project development; 5. to develop skills of video filming in nature and indoors, under natural and artificial lighting; 6. to develop skills of quality sound recording, processing and mixing; 7. to develop skills of video editing, post-processing and publishing video on the Internet; 8. to develop skills to plan and organize live video streaming.
independent_study: Students will study the online study course content (MOOCs, webinars, lecture notes and handouts) and prepare home-works and participate in tests independently. There will be practical workshops where students will work on the preproduction, production and postproduction of a video. During the study course, students have to prepare a production plan for a short film, shoot the video, do post-production activities and publish it on YouTube. All students will have an opportunity to ask questions online and take part in discussion forums. It is expected that students will learn from the online study course content before class. This will thus be allowing them to focus on practical activities and preparation of the film during the face-to-face sessions.

title: Marketing and Digital Transformation
abstract: The study course provides an in-depth understanding of the impact of digital transformation on the effective development of business environment, marketing and organizational communication.
aims: The aim of the study course is to systematize and deepen the students' knowledge of the impact of marketing and digital transformation on the operation of the organization, to promote the application of acquired knowledge, skills and methodological abilities in the development of the organization. Objectives: • To develop students' understanding of business digitization processes; • To develop students' ability to analyze modern marketing opportunities, communication ecosystems and determine their practical use; • To develop students' ability to generate, group, select, evaluate and use different approaches to marketing and digitization; • To develop theoretical and practical knowledge of structured marketing planning, segmentation of target audience, methods of communication and marketing technology management and their application possibilities; • To promote the development of applied skills, including the ability to present individual ideas in a reasoned manner, collaborate in a team.
independent_study: Independent work includes the development of an individual strategic marketing plan and solving case studies in practical classes.

title: Product Design and Development
status_in_programme: Compulsory/Courses of Limited Choice; Courses of Free Choice
abstract: The focus of the course is integration of the marketing, design and manufacturing functions of the firm in creating a new product/service. The course is intended to provide students with a set of tools and methods for product design and development. During the course students will develop a real prototype of a new product/service.
aims: The goal of the course is to systematize and broaden knowledge and develop practical skills in new product development and with an aim to apply this knowledge and skills in professional situations and everyday activities. Main task of the course is to develop competences in new product planning and development, and to apply this in practice, to stimulate skills of creativity, planning and presentation.
independent_study: The course is based on formation of project groups (4-6 members of the project group), who during the course are working on practical project. Project contains 5 assignments, development of prototype and presentation of the project results. Each assignment will be evaluated by grade in 10 point scale. Final grade for the course composes from: 70% evaluation of assignments; 30% evaluation of the prototype and final project presentation.

title: Fundamentals of 3D Graphics Modeling and Animation
abstract: During the study course, the students will learn the basics of three-dimensional (3D) objects modelling and animation using the existing 3D graphic modelling software. The software allows modelling, modification and animation of 3D objects, creation of textures, implementation of light sources and combination of acquired resources into 3D scenes. The basics of 3D graphics modelling will be taught, beginning with simple primitive objects to complex realistic characters. The students will also learn the basics of animation and will be able to apply realistic animation to 3D objects and combine characters, objects and scenes to create a 3D video animation. The objects and characters created during the study course can be further used for various tasks, like the creation of interactive scenes, special effects for video films, adding characters to computer games, etc.
aims: The goal of the study course is to provide theoretical knowledge and practical skills in the modelling and animation of 3D objects. The tasks of the study course are: 1. To provide theoretical knowledge about the structure of 3D objects and characters, the basics of their modelling. 2. To provide theoretical knowledge about the basics of the 3D object and character animation. 3. To develop practical skills to apply theoretical knowledge to modelling and animation of 3D models (objects, scenes, characters).
independent_study: Independent work is integrated with the learning of theoretical material and the performance of practical tasks. During the practical lessons, students realize three-dimensional scenes of various complexity, which are based on the material discussed during the lesson. After the lesson, independent work is given, where students need to supplement a started three-dimensional scene or animation depending on a defined task. The independent work is closely related to the modelling and texturing tools and materials covered during the lesson. The tasks of independent work are to deepen students' knowledge in 3D modelling and animation, as well as to analyze with which tools and according to which methodologies complex scenes, texturing objects and creating special effects can be created.

title: Architectural Morphology in Digital Humanities
abstract: The study course is focused on the acquisition of the interconnections of the structure of the spatial environment and its constituent elements. Regional, national and international influences, spatial, economic and social factors and groups involved in creating a sustainable environment are considered. Within the study course, students get acquainted with the philosophical and research aspects of the art of creating an environment; basic principles of morphological analysis; the role of social processes and functions in shaping, ecological and contextual approach, as well as tools and methods of public interpretation of scientific research activities.
aims: The aim of the study course is to develop students' understanding of the role of the art of creating an environment in the creation of living space in society in the modern information technology age. The tasks of the study course are: - to develop an understanding of the interdisciplinary nature of spatial environment formation; - to evolve the ability to evaluate the impact of functional, aesthetic, political, economic and social processes on specific environmental development factors; - to advance the ability to choose adequate and purposeful means and methods for the problem.
independent_study: To develop the application of the research project, selecting the theme, characterizing its topicality and present state of knowledge, defining the problem, goals and objectives, selected research methods, novelty of the research and ways of application of the results.

title: Introduction to Programming, Design of E-learning Materials and Education Technologies
abstract: During the study course, students will be introduced to interactive e-learning material development technologies in education and distance learning, as well as the necessary basic skills in programming. The content of the study course consists of two parts. The first part of the study course teaches students to quickly start and apply basic programming skills to create a computer game by applying object-oriented concepts. The study course brings the physical dimension of experiences to integrate within the game application being developed. The study course is intended to give a glimpse of how a programming language be used to practically implement an idea, so that, students with or without programming experience can start off working with various aspects of digital technology. In the second part, students will explore multidisciplinary interconnections between pedagogy, technology, cognitive science, graphic design, software engineering, and human-computer interaction. Students will be introduced to the best practice of online education and e-learning development and delivery. They will practice the creation of a variety of e-learning materials and activity types as well as the meaningful application of associated learning theories.
aims: The aim of the study course is to enhance students’ perspectives and views of programming, technology as it relates to teaching, learning, and training, as well as to enhance their skills of e-learning development and application. The tasks of the study course are: 1. to develop skills in Python programming; 2. to improve students' understanding of the modelling of physical processes in software; 3. to develop skills for creating an interactive game using object-oriented programming language; 4. to develop skills of planning, structuring and implementing multimedia e-learning objects. 5. to teach to identify and evaluate current and future technologies for use in education; 6. to encourage the ability to find and apply effective strategies and technology tools to support learning; 7. to teach designing and developing assessment activities allowing assessment of student's progress; 8. to promote the use of multimedia for the development of interactive teaching materials; 9. to promote the use of learning management systems.
independent_study: Learning from educational multimedia. Taking tests. Doing activities. Practical work in programming. Group work. Collaborative work. Practical work in e-learning module planning and development.

title: Scientific Modelling
abstract: The study course is included in the master study programme for students of the Faculty of Humanities and e- learning technologies who have not mastered engineering at the bachelor's level. The study course provides a transdisciplinary approach to knowledge, skills and competencies. Students acquire basic extract of the knowledge, developing a holistic view of the fundamental processes in nature in the framework of physics, environmental sciences and biology. The subject of the study course includes basic relationships in the scale from the universe to the microcosm on the atomic level and human as a substantial component of it. At the same time, students acquire a comprehension of digital modelling of the natural science processes and interconnections – graphics, diagrams, multimedia models and video explanations. Students will acquire skills of models’ practical design. The study course will develop students’ comprehension of the pedagogical efficiency of the natural science models, to assess and systematize models according to pedagogical effectiveness.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide an understanding of the development of models of natural sciences used in education and to teach their practical development and use in accordance with different pedagogical approaches, based on online resources. The tasks of the study course are: 1) to provide theoretical knowledge and understanding of the following topics: - solutions of digital technologies for the creation of a holistic understanding of natural processes; - digital solutions of natural processes modelling in accordance with findings of sustainable pedagogy and psychology; - critical comprehension of use of digital modelling; - types of natural processes models, systematization, standards and application. 2) to develop the following skills: - to exercise suitable natural processes models in contemporary e-learning environments in accordance with findings of pedagogy and psychology of knowledge society. - to choose the most appropriate type and tool for modeling natural processes and to create digital teaching material; 3) to teach competencies to create educational and holistic digital content teaching materials with an understanding of the course of natural processes.
independent_study: Students must study learning material, available in the e-learning environment. They must get involved in discussions, and take 8 internet tests. Students must design their own course assessment on the natural sciences, including natural science models. They must assess in accordance with evaluation criteria, and express complementary ideas on improvements of no less than 2 course mates’ assessments.

title: Python Programming Language
status_in_programme: Compulsory/Courses of Limited Choice; Courses of Free Choice
abstract: Within the study course, students are introduced to the possibilities of the programming language Python and the principles of software development. The study course provides an introduction to the programming language Python and its use in solving practical tasks. The study course covers the stages of software development, program structure, cyclic constructions, functions, procedures, arrays, symbol strings, text files, objects, as well as the use of libraries to solve specialization-related tasks. The study course also covers the use of Python modules, which allow students to add to the functionality of the programming language by reducing software development time and program code length. Upon completion of the study course, students will gain knowledge and practical experience that will allow them to use Python to solve typical tasks in their field of specialization.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide students with the basics of programming in Python and develop their awareness of the possibilities of its use for solving various tasks related to the field of study. Tasks of the study course: * to ensure mastering of software development stages; * to ensure the mastering of the principles of Python language syntax, construction, and program structure; * to ensure the acquisition of input data control, information integrity checks, task automation basics and user interface design; * to ensure the acquisition of the possibilities of using external resources for solving certain tasks.
independent_study: Students get ready for the laboratory works, perform exercises and independent tasks using development environments designed for specific tasks.

title: Theory and Practice of Natural Language Processing
abstract: Natural language processing is an interdisciplinary field that studies methods and models enabling computers to process, understand, and generate human (natural) language. Within the study course, students learn the main concepts of natural language processing, its various practical applications and the methods used to implement them, as well as the skills for evaluation and interpretation of the obtained results. For solving practical natural language processing tasks, students learn appropriate software tools.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge in natural language processing and its practical applications. The tasks of the study course: - to develop students’ understanding of the basic concepts of natural language processing and the tasks it solves; - to develop students’ skills to identify and choose natural language processing methods suitable for solving specific tasks; - to improve students’ skills to apply these methods in practice, as well as to evaluate and interpret the obtained results; - to develop students’ skills to use software tools appropriate to specific natural language processing problems.
independent_study: Individual assignments involve solving theoretical and practical tasks where students apply the knowledge acquired during the study course on natural language processing, its methods, and appropriate software tools.

title: Terminology and Terminography
abstract: The study course provides students with information on terminology creation, application and alignment, as well as terminography management systems. The study course introduces information about planning activities and electronic management of terminology, which spans a range of interdependent phases, such as organizing documentation and capturing data from running text, storing, editing, maintaining and updating data using various data structures. Throughout the study course, students are encouraged to broaden their individual knowledge and understanding of the study course as well as to undertake independent reading both to supplement and consolidate what is being taught. Students share the samples of compiling personal term data bank for peer evaluation and discuss successful term creation strategies, common difficulties, and the ways of solving a variety of terminology alignment related issues.
aims: The primary goal of the study course is to expand the students’ knowledge of both the design and user possibilities of terminology application and its management systems. Particular attention will be paid to new and developing subject areas such as knowledge representation and transfer, meaning-formation and term-creation patterns, information technology tools, expert systems and terminological databases. Objectives of the study course: • to develop student skills to critically examine the concept of ‘term’ and the possibilities of meaning description; • to acquaint students with the principles of traditional terminology and promote their interest in the research of the new directions; • to develop student skills to analyse the methods and principles of modern theories of terminology and terminography.
independent_study: Developing individual learning strategies for mastering conventions of term-formation; presenting personal term bank in the respective scientific technical field with text samples from various sources.

title: Technologies for Digitisation of Culture Heritage objects
abstract: The study course includes a general insight into the acquisition of geometric information on Culture Heritage objects using photogrammetry, laser scanning, image processing and other methods of obtaining geometric information. The study course deals with the principles of documenting historical objects, applied methods, graphic formats in 2D and 3D graphic environments. Also, the possibilities of creating an information system for cultural and historical objects, making the objects virtually accessible to the general public, are considered.
aims: The aim of the study course is to acquaint students with various methods of digitization of cultural objects and preparation of historical research data for the further research process. The tasks of the study course are: 1. To provide knowledge about cultural and historical objects, their significance in culture. 2. To form an understanding of the methods of obtaining geometric information. 3. To provide knowledge and to develop an understanding of the creation of a digital 3D model. 4. To develop skills for applying digital results in Virtual Devices. 5. To develop social skills: group work, critical thinking, problem-solving skills. 6. To provide information on the use of data on areas for sustainable development and integration of social culture.
independent_study: Each student carries out research work with literature, preparation of a report, documentation of a small object and virtual representation of the results. During the study process, documentation of a cultural-historical object and production of a 3D model is performed.

title: Linguistic Analysis of Visual Culture
abstract: The study course is intended for the master level students of either engineering or humanities study programs and is aimed at investigating the historical and contemporary dimensions of diverse visual culture from a linguistic perspective, exploring it from aesthetic, critical, literary, and experiential viewpoints. The students are expected to benefit greatly from an intellectually-rigorous study environment, which is intended to boost their interdisciplinary thinking and explore new levels of cultural and linguistic awareness. Exploring the facets of visual culture through the prism of linguistic analysis, the students are going to develop better visual literacy, understand the linkage between language and the forms of visual culture, get acquainted with the different forms of visual culture, analyse these issues in a multilingual and multicultural environment, learn the concept of intermediality and its role on the perception of societal activities. The balance between the theoretical and practical classes is attained across a range of topics, including: contemporary visual culture, analysis of visual culture disciplines, avant-garde visual culture activities, i.e. comics and videogaming, digital tools of its analysis, visualism and imagery in media and advertisement, linguistic analysis of different visual culture instances, visual metaphor, different manifestations of visual art.
aims: The aim of the study course is to introduce students to a wide range of ongoing debates on the study and the role of visual culture in modern society. The tasks of the study course: 1) to acquaint the students with the theoretical premises of Anglo-Saxon and German origin, comparing the notions of visual culture and image science 2) to develop students’ skills to empirically analyse different case studies investigating the connection of visualiasm and language; 3) to develop students' conceptual framework in which they should be able to assess the manifestations of different instances of visual culture in different linguistic instances and their common role in contemporary society; 3) to provide students with information on how different forms of visual culture produce and shape meanings and how these meanings are further created, expressed, analysed, understood, transferred by the means of linguistic tools.
independent_study: Analysing interconnection between different manifestations of visual culture and language tools; exploring how the meaning is constructed in visual culture and how it gets interpreted in written speech; submitting individually developed case studies.

title: Digital Rhetoric
abstract: The study course introduces the fundamental notions of Digital Rhetoric, it covers the main themes of digital rhetoric: classical rhetoric, visual rhetoric, human-computer interaction, the survey of theories on digital rhetoric, network rhetoric.
aims: The goal of the study course is to teach students the fundamentals of digital rhetoric. Objectives of the study course: 1. to define the subject of digital rhetoric; 2. to develop student ability to investigate the theories of digital rhetoric; 3. to acquaint students with digital rhetoric and its relation to classical rhetoric theory; 4. to introduce definitions, approaches and methods of studies; 5. to develop student skills to analyse rhetoric functions of the media and new media, human-computer interaction (HCI), and other interdisciplinary fields including Internet studies.
independent_study: Regular, individual work with theoretical literature and other information sources. Report on application of digital rhetoric.

title: Introduction to Data Corpus Analysis in Humanities
abstract: Interdisciplinary insights are essential for realizing the full potential of corpus-assisted analysis methods that deal with processing rich social and cultural data. In order to capture a range of ideas and identify commonalities that resonate with the body of research in the field, within the study course it is planned to consider different approaches to corpus-assisted studies in humanities. The study course covers a set of crucial questions in corpus studies, including conceptualisation, data selection and operationalisation, analysis and interpretation of results. The study course consists of two blocks covering the theory and practice of corpus compilation and processing. In the theoretical part, students are invited to consider a number of diverse case studies and analyse the problems of building different types of corpora. The practical part is devoted to experiments with the corpus of fanfics (i.e., amateur interpretations of commercial texts) explicitly tailored for the needs of the study course. The selected research material allows scholars of different backgrounds and pursuing different research interests (such as socio-linguistics, media studies, translation studies, literary studies, and anthropology) to analyse research questions on its basis.
aims: The aims of the study course are to introduce students: * to different approaches to corpus-assisted studies in humanities; * to the main aspects and problems of corpora creation. The tasks of the study course are to develop students' ability: * to observe cultural trends and subject them to the quantitative investigation; * to conduct interdisciplinary research; * to conduct corpus analysis.
independent_study: Getting ready for two seminars where students will have to demonstrate a critical understanding of academic texts in the field of corpus-assisted studies in humanities; independent research project made based on students' corpora; small report and presentation of the project.

title: Research of Culture, Language and Technology Synergy in Latvia
abstract: The main emphasis of the study course is made on the interaction between culture, language, and technology in Latvia in the historical perspective and today. The study course provides an overview of sculpture, painting, literature in the territory of Latvia as being a result of the synergy of historical processes.
aims: The aim of the study course: to ensure students acquire theoretical knowledge and develop their practical skills about the interaction between culture, language, and technology in the territory of Latvia over the centuries. The objectives of the study course: 1. To develop students’ understanding of the terms and methods used in culture, language, and technology interaction. 2. To develop students’ presentation skills using digital technologies that can be used practically to inform the society.

title: Digital Semantics and Pragmatics
abstract: The study course is primarily aimed at developing advanced and highly specialized proficiency level competences and skills of the students mastering study programmes in humanities, interdisciplinary STEM+, and information technology. Along with a comprehensive overview of the fundamental issues associated with the retrieval, collection, organization, and processing of semantic and pragmatic data (semantic and thematic fields, meaning representation, meaning extension, conceptual mapping, and ontology building, discourse and truth- value analysis), students will get acquainted with the state-of-the-art in the area of natural language processing (NLP) and natural language generation (NLG), which will help them establish a comprehensive theoretical framework for performing a variety of NLP and NLG-related tasks. Throughout a series of video lectures, independent reading activities, and extensive practical training, students will learn to organize and represent unstructured and semi-structured linguistic data for further use in various text mining, information retrieval, and knowledge management applications. Students will study the foundations of compositional and distributional semantics, learn to analyse the topic structure and develop their competence to build semantic models, i.e., semantic networks, taxonomies, ontologies and knowledge graphs, and customize and apply existing ones. Upon completion of the study course, students will be able to participate in the work of various NLP technology development teams, conduct research in the field of digital semantics and pragmatics, and solve a range of knowledge management tasks, as well as create solutions to complex problems with limited definition that are related to modifying, refining, improving and integrating new content and information into existing knowledge of digital semantics and pragmatics to create new and original ideas. Students will be able to participate in the creation and adaptation of lexicographic resources to the needs of individual industries, particular SMEs and start-ups in the development of new products and services with high added value.
aims: Goals of the study course: - to ensure students develop a comprehensive knowledge of semantic relationships, categorial grammar, and meaning representation models to be able to compile, maintain, and customize digital lexicographic (e.g., WordNet dictionaries, semantic networks, ontologies, knowledge graphs, etc.) and text processing resources; - to develop student’s competence in selecting, using, and customizing relevant language technologies for retrieval, collection, organization, storage, and representation of semantic and pragmatic data; - to develop student’s competence in co-constructing and co-creating semantic and pragmatic data, resources, and context-specific knowledge. Objectives of the study course: - to advance student’s skills in developing, adjusting, and applying digital semantic, pragmatic, and syntactic models for word sense representation and analysis; - to develop student’s ability to understand working principles of related NLP technologies and apply them to process unstructured and semi-structured semantic data for various applications; - to develop student’s competence in using knowledge graphs, word sense taxonomies, and distributional semantic models to organize and represent semantic and pragmatic data; - to develop student’s competence in using natural language generation tools for various domains; - to advance student’s ability to cooperate in proposing and creating solutions to interdisciplinary semantics and pragmatics-rooted language technology challenges of various complexity levels with limited definition using digital tools and possible technological responses, and to adapt and customize digital environments to personal needs.
independent_study: Students shall independently get acquainted with a comprehensive body of relevant literature and engage in extensive hands-on training, which will provide them with professional knowledge and competence in the selection and application of language technologies for compiling, organizing, representing, and managing linguistic data. The study course was developed within the Language Technology Initiative project 2.3.1.1.i./0/1/22/I/CFLA/002 LU RN ESS2023/453, and in the validation and piloting stage is delivered as a MOOC. The study course is available upon registration at https://mooc.rtu.lv/courses/digital-semantics-and- pragmatics/.

title: Multimodal Digital Semiotics
abstract: The study course is primarily aimed at developing advanced and highly specialized proficiency level competences and skills of the students mastering study programmes in humanities, interdisciplinary STEM+ based, and information technology. The study course promotes students' awareness of various linguistic and non- linguistic semiotic systems and helps them develop a comprehensive understanding of the current trends in their change and development under the influence of digital technologies and media. Upon completion of the study course, students will advance their knowledge of various sign systems, textual interactions, conceptual relations, spatial relations, sequential relations, and syntagmatic and paradigmatic dimensions of signification. Students will develop advanced competence in creating and disseminating multimodal content via digital media, they will also establish a sound competence for the development, customization, and maintenance of digital semiotic resources. The syllabus of the study course has been balanced to cover a range of theoretical and applied issues to demonstrate the added value of integrating language technology-instigated solutions in the development, customization, and maintenance of multimodal digital semiotic resources. Through a series of lectures, workshops, and practical classes, students will learn to cooperate in proposing and creating solutions to interdisciplinary semiotic language technology-related challenges of various complexity level with limited definition associated with creation, edition and dissemination of digital content in different formats, and self- expression through digital means. Students will develop awareness of the added value that the methods and tools of Multimodal Digital Semiotics may ensure in multimodal digital content creation, digital editing and publishing, development and localization of games, digital advertising, and semiotic data management. It will ultimately increase the employability of the students and help them come up with cost-efficient solutions meeting the needs of the interdisciplinary STEM+ industry and individual SMEs. Students will be motivated to integrate the acquired interdisciplinary knowledge and to contribute within the scope of the gained professional competencies to guide others in interaction and sharing through digital technologies. Methods and tools of Multimodal Digital Semiotics present a new scientific method of studying language and other sign systems for research, development, and co-development of knowledge management and knowledge representation models, systems, and solutions in communication sciences, computer science, and across STEM+ areas.
aims: Goals of the study course: - to advance student knowledge of linguistic and non-linguistic semiotic systems, various aspects of efficient coding, representation, and communication of meaning in the multimodal digital environment; - to develop student competence in integrating language technology-instigated solutions in the development, customization, and maintenance of multimodal digital semiotic resources; - to develop student skills in using and customization of relevant digital semiotic resources for cost-efficient solutions to industry-related challenges. Objectives of the study course: - to promote student understanding of key concepts of semiotics and the role of multimodal semiotic resources in creating added value; - to develop student skills to create and disseminate high-quality multimodal content via digital media; - to develop student skills to select, use, develop, customize, and maintain multimodal digital semiotic resources to solve practical tasks in such areas as digital content creation, digital advertising, gaming, digital editing, and publishing, etc.; - to advance student competence and willingness to cooperate in proposing and creating solutions to interdisciplinary semiotic language technology-related challenges of various complexity level with limited definition associated with creation, edition and dissemination of digital content in different formats, and self- expression through digital means.
independent_study: Students should independently get acquainted with a comprehensive body of relevant literature. Students should develop and/or customize an emulated digital semiotic resource to solve a real industry-related task. The study course was developed within the Language Technology Initiative project 2.3.1.1.i./0/1/22/I/CFLA/002 LU RN ESS2023/453, and in the validation and piloting stage is delivered as a MOOC. title: Digital Sentiment Analysis
abstract: The study course is primarily aimed at developing advanced and highly specialized proficiency level competences and skills of the students mastering study programs in humanities, interdisciplinary STEM+ based, and information technology. The study course is envisioned for post-graduate students with the basic knowledge of natural language processing (NLP) willing to advance their competence in sentiment analysis and textual data processing for a variety of applied industry-related tasks. Students will learn to classify unstructured and semi- structured data to determine sentiment polarity (i.e., either positive, negative, or neutral) with the help of free and commercial tools that they will customize for their own research, learning, and occupational needs. Students learn to retrieve and select sentiment-related characteristics and contextual features using relevant models and to assess the impact of the emotion-related words on the overall sentiment of the analysed text. Students will develop skills to extract the semantic information from the text, to analyse, classify and evaluate it in terms of sentiment for improving customer experience and quality assurance purposes. Students will master speech tagging, noun phrase extraction, emotion detection, and sentiment analysis, and will address such notions as polarity, intentions and subjectivity by practically working with Python and its dedicated libraries for sentiment analysis, e.g., NLTK and TextBlob. In the practical assignments, students will implement lexicon-based sentiment analysis (e.g., using the VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) lexicon), use pre-trained models for sentiment identification (e.g., the RoBERTa model) and other solutions such as Matplotlib library for the visualization and evaluations of sentiment analysis results. Given the added value sentiment analysis can ensure in the analysis of marketing data, e-commerce, public opinion polling, business intelligence, policy planning, education efficiency assessment, and other fields, the competencies and skills students will develop within the study course will contribute to their professional practices and employability and help them solve topical industry challenges.
aims: Goals of the study course: - to develop student’s knowledge about the key concepts of sentiment analysis, e.g., polarity, intentions and subjectivity, bi-grams, tri-grams, and n-grams; - to develop student’s knowledge in the normalizations and representation of a text using various methods, e.g., Bag-of-Words, TF-IDF, etc.; - to establish student’s competence to develop, customize, and test trained models for sentiment analysis using relevant software. Objectives of the study course: - to advance student’s skills to preprocess and analyse data for sentiment analysis; - to develop student’s skills to practically perform text tokenization, lemmatization, noise cleaning, stopwords filtering, etc.; - to develop student’s skills to retrieve and analyse n-grams; - to develop student’s ability to relate word vectors to the classification of sentiment; - to develop student’s ability to cooperate in proposing and creating solutions to interdisciplinary language technology challenges of various complexity levels with limited definition which are related to wise, risks minimizing usage of digital technologies on people and environment, including their use for social well-being and social integration; - to develop student’s awareness of the ethical aspects of conducting sentiment analysis and sustainable and ethical application thereof.

title: Digital Ethics and Artificial Intelligence Interaction
status_in_programme: Compulsory/Courses of Limited Choice; Courses of Free Choice
abstract: The study course provides an in-depth insight into the conceptual foundations of digital ethics and their connection with the architecture and application of large language models (LLM) in artificial intelligence (AI). Special attention is paid to the main principles of digital ethics, safe and responsible behavior in virtual space, as well as the technical aspects of large language models, their architecture, training processes, the importance of data quality, and practical applications, which simultaneously create new opportunities for innovation and serious ethical challenges. The study course combines theoretical understanding of ethical paradigms and artificial intelligence architecture with practical tasks in case analysis and critical evaluation.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide students with knowledge of ethics and the operating principles of large language models in artificial intelligence, to develop students' ability to combine the theoretical foundations of digital ethics with a technical understanding of AI, critically evaluating their interaction. Objectives of the study course: - to provide in-depth knowledge of the ethical theories and principles that govern the use of technology; - to teach about architecture, operating mechanisms, and training processes of large language models; - to develop the ability to theoretically and practically apply the principles of digital ethics in the analysis and use of AI solutions in various industries; - to promote students' abilities and competencies in creating scenarios for the use of large language models, integrating technical and ethical knowledge.
independent_study: Independent work by students includes analytical work with educational literature and other sources of information, individual and group tasks, and case study solutions.

title: Introduction to Knowledge Society Technology
abstract: The knowledge society is in bases of all modern innovations and knowledge development since the beginning of the 21st century. In this study course, we are going to learn about the actual knowledge of technologies in society being used, developed from the second half of the 20th century to nowadays. During the study course, students will get acquainted with the principles of operation of computers, data networks; their structure, and physical processes in communication technologies. After completing the study course, students will be able to explain the principles of operation of a computer and its functional components. The study course will also provide an intuitive overview of computer data input and output interfaces, physical processes in them, as well as conceptual methods used to control data flow. During the study course, students will refresh understanding of binary and hexadecimal counting systems, which also will help to build a strong foundation in the understanding of computers operations. Students will gain insight into the physical processes and organizational liabilities that ensure the existence of information and data communications technologies. Also, the main computers operating systems used in practice will be discussed. The basic principles of maintenance of secure digital operating environments to avoid computer viruses and malware will be explained. Even more, the study course provides an insight into the elements of signal theory to understand principles of data communication in dense electrically conductive media, light-conducting optical media, and wireless or vacuum environments. During the study course, students will also get acquainted with currently used multimedia technologies (like digital footage making, and audio production), hidden tools under the hood of WEB browsers, and other useful utilities. At the end of the study course, the development trends of knowledge society technologies will be considered.
aims: The study course aim is to provide the acquisition of updated and reliable information, hand-on-experience enabling building of creative, efficient, and qualitative knowledge and skills of how-to-use modern computers, data networks, and principles of signal transmission. The tasks of the study course are to provide conditions, transfer experience and provide information for the improvement of knowledge about computer systems, data networks, as well as the principles of operation and construction of data interfaces. Practised tasks help to form a new understanding of the importance of software layer for the operation of computer systems, as well as the basic methods of safe data retrieval, processing, presentation, transmission, and storage. The study course task list includes knowledge gaining on basic principles of data and computer network security, as well as familiarity explaining the physical principles and concepts of IT and communication technologies. Also, one of the study course tasks provides hands-on-experience in organizing essential "client- server" type communication using standard WEB browser and some extra utilities.
independent_study: Students individually recover study materials in the virtual study course environment and perform assigned tasks. Students have an opportunity to test their knowledge, skills and abilities solving practical exercises. Students must learn to choose relevant IT solutions based on the set of optimal criteria. Study course participant have the opportunity to mail with staff and participate in discussion forums communicating with course mates. It is expected that the study course participants will study ongoing learning materials before the current face-to- face lesson. Thus, the flipped-classroom method allows focusing on practical work and solving current thematic tasks efficiently.

title: E-pedagogy and e-didactics
abstract: The study course provides students with a comprehensive overview of a range of issues topical the digital age: e- pedagogy and its essence; development of pedagogical competencies to be applied in working with digital media and technologies; digital identities, their development; learning through internet; pedagogic-didactic implications of internet use; the internet as a learning medium; didactics of vocational education.
aims: The aim of the study course is to develop sound background knowledge of the students and raise their awareness about categories, principles and regularities of e-pedagogy and didactics. The tasks of the course: • to encourage students to master the methods, forms and tools of e-pedagogy and didactics for digital humanities applications; • to develop student understanding of the learning theories, their representation in the e-learning process and use of digital media for educational purposes; • to develop students’ pedagogical skills to facilitate the creation of the digital identity of pupils and students.
independent_study: Students have to study relevant literature and complete an individual task “Curriculum Design Methodology of a Lecture/Practical Class”. The paper should demonstrate student’s knowledge and skills in planning a lecture/practical class and curriculum design on an e-pedagogy and didactics platform.

title: Media and Society
abstract: Within this study course, students analyze the influence of media on the mass consciousness and the behavior of indivuduals developing the skills to use critical discourse analysis (CDA) in researching media content. Special attention is paid to the possible manipulations with mass consciousness. Within the course several communication theories and the possibilities to use them in research practice discussed. Special emphasis is made on data protection and information reliability on the internet.
aims: The goal of the study course is to provide the students with the basic competencies to enable them to conduct qualified media critical discourse analysis fulfilling their professional duties. Within this course students develop skills to evaluate the reliability of information, to recognize manipulative methods and to apprehend the ethical aspects of media content.
independent_study: In order to gain credits for the course it is required to fulfil the following independent tasks: 1) the study of relevant literature; 2) tests; 3) exercises; 4) discussions at seminars; 5) practical assignments.

title: Cognitive and Social Psychology
abstract: The study course covers the basic principles of cognitive and social psychology, with an emphasis on social cognition and its practical application in everyday professional and personal activities. The study course is arranged in three parts, where the first one focuses on social psychology, the second part reviews cognitive processes, the third part emphasizes social cognition. Throughout the lecture course, students understand how cognitive processes affect social processes and vice versa, also viewing them in correlation with virtual environment. At the end of the study course, students know the interaction of cognitive and social processes, holds methods of managing these processes and are able to make socially responsible decisions in carrying out effective cognitive and social functioning. Various teaching methods are used in the acquisition of the study course - case studies, discussions, surveys and tests, presentations, group work, videos, etc. audience engagement techniques.
aims: The aim of the study course is to develop an understanding of the basic concepts of social cognition, the interaction of social and cognitive psychology and how they affect everyday life and professional activities, so that students can effectively and socially responsibly analyze and interpret social and cognitive processes in everyday life and professional life by addressing current psychological issues. Tasks of the study course: 1. To form an understanding of the main constructs of social and cognitive psychology, currently relevant, their mutual interaction, emphasizing the virtual environment. 2. To improve the skills to distinguish the processes of social psychology from the cognitive ones and to choose appropriate methods for the research, analysis, and improvement of these processes. 3. To promote students' self-assessment, personal growth, development of cognitive processes and responsibility in the improvement of social processes by reviewing case studies and practical work. 4. To promote the competence to recognize the surrounding and one's own strengths and development opportunities in the context of social cognition, to apply correct methods in acting on one's own and other people's potential in a socially responsible and ethical way. 5. To develop an understanding about the features of user-friendly, evidence-based products and services and their ethical use.
independent_study: Autonomous work is organized at the lectures and in the e-learning environment using lecture notes and texts prepared by the instructor. Individual work is aimed at developing skills for self-analysis and ability to recognize psychological problems in texts or personal experience.

title: Internship
abstract: The internship is aimed at practically strengthening the acquired theoretical knowledge and skills working in the interdisciplinary field of Digital Humanities. It is conducted according to the individual assignment elaborated jointly by the student, university and a company. The internship includes establishing theoretical foundations in the work area, execution of the tasks from the individual assignment and preparation of the internship report.
aims: Fieldwork/internship is an essential part of the study programme aimed at improving the professional skills and competencies of the student in the professional environment, as well as advancing and improving their knowledge in digital humanities related fields. The tasks of the fieldwork, which are assigned to each student individually, include but are not limited to: • development, practical application and approbation of a technology, web application or model; • analysis of the challenges pertaining to meaning representation exploiting, tailoring, approbating and developing technology, web application or model; • development of innovative solutions in Digital Humanities: multimodal content creation, graphic design, cartography, archive digitalization, etc.; • representation, processing and transfer of multimodal and intersemiotic information; • graphic data analysis and visualisation; • building a professional network; • establishment of a professional track record; • getting familiarised with the industry standards and legislation; • building awareness of sustainable, ethical and inclusive business practices; • getting familiarised with the code of professional ethics.
independent_study: The tasks of an internship, a set of planned activities as well as the deadline for each assignment are formulated individually. The Supervisor of the Internship should make sure that the tasks are set in accordance with the latest development trends in the given industry. The student contacts both the Supervisor and the Internship Coordinator on the regular basis for a relevant updates on the results and challenges faced within the framework of the internship.

title: Master Thesis
abstract: Upon completion of the master study programme, students shall pass a state examination, which is assessed according to a 10-grade scale. Viva Voce of the Master Thesis makes part of the state examination. The Master Thesis amounting to 20 credit points consists of the theoretical and empirical/analytical parts (project). In the theoretical part of the Master Thesis, students investigate a selected issue in the field of digital humanities and provide an overview of the relevant theoretical literature, substantiate the topicality of the chosen theme and analyse its impact on the development of the field. The empirical/analytical (project) part of the Master Thesis presents a case study on: 1) the challenges of meaning representation exploiting, tailoring, approbating and developing technology, web applications or model; 2) the challenges associated with preservation, management and digitization of cultural heritage; 3) the development, analysis, practical application and approbation of technology, web application, mobile app or various models, e.g., a description of a developed e-learning course, applied software, web page development project, etc.; 4) the challenges in representation, processing and transfer of multimodal and intersemiotic information; 5) storage and archiving of multimedia information; 6) graphical analysis and visualization of data; 7) introduction and incorporation of edutainment principles into modern educational models and social activities, etc. Students develop their Master Theses independently in accordance with the study plan during the last semester of their studies consulting both the supervisor and, if necessary, a specialist in the respective field.
aims: The aim of the study course is to provide students with an opportunity to attest to the set of skills and competencies they have developed having mastered the master study programme “Digital Humanities”. Tasks of the study course: • to help students demonstrate their research and analytical skills developing a theoretical part of their Master Thesis; • to motivate students to apply skills in digital humanities acquired within the framework of the Master study Program for analysing challenges in the chosen professional area; • to improve students’ scientific writing skills; • to consolidate students’ skills of identification and solving of interdisciplinary problems in the field of Digital Humanities and the skills of delivering academic presentations.
